what: Overdrive: it pushes a sound until it starts to distort, like a guitar amplifier turned up loud. It makes a sound warmer, thicker and rougher.
how: The DRIVE knob amplifies the sound into a soft limiter that rounds the tops of the wave, which adds harmonics (extra overtones) and a feeling of loudness. Soft means the change is gradual: a little drive adds warmth, a lot is fuzzy and grainy. LEVEL sets the volume afterwards, since more drive usually means a louder result.

outs.out: The overdriven sound, set by LEVEL. Patch it into a filter, an effect or OUT.

knobs.drive: How much distortion: 0 is almost clean, 1 is heavy fuzz.
knobs.level: Volume of the result: 0 is silent, 1 is full, 1.5 is louder. Turn it down if more drive makes it too loud.

try: Patch VCO (SAW) into DRIVE's in and DRIVE's out into OUT's left. Play a note and turn DRIVE up slowly: the tone gets thicker and grittier. Then turn LEVEL down to compare at the same loudness.
